rounds.text: Acme India Industries Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of just 11.2x [E1], representing a stark discount against the sector benchmark P/E of 18.13x [E5]. The company demonstrates elite capital efficiency, boasting an exceptional ROE of 30.62% [E8] and a robust ROCE of 28.18% [E9], both of which obliterate sector benchmarks of 5.39% [E8] and 6.7% [E9] respectively. Top-line and bottom-line expansions are firing on all cylinders, evidenced by trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 26% [E13] and profit growth of 45% [E14], handily outpacing sector medians of 13.3% [E46] and 17.7% [E45]. Operating margins have steadily climbed over the last four years [E18], expanding by 6 percentage points from 10% three years ago to 16% in Mar 2026 [E17], all supported by a favorable sector tailwind score of +0.63 [E44]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 232 per share compared to a market price of Rs 164 [E31], offering a substantial margin of safety of 29.3% [E32], while a reverse DCF reveals the current market price only prices in a modest 5.2% earnings growth against the 10.0% base case [E33]. Conceded: [E20], [E21], [E22], [E23], [E25], [E37].

Despite robust headline returns, the company suffers from severe cash generation and working capital distress that undermine its reported profits. Operating cash flow and free cash flow for March 2026 are both deeply negative at minus 12 crore rupees, resulting in a troubling cash conversion ratio of minus 0.50x against reported profit [E20, E21, E22]. This alarming disconnect between earnings and actual cash is further compounded by exceptionally high debtors stretching to 349 days [E37]. To fund operations amid this cash drain, borrowings have escalated to 119 crore rupees as of September 2026, up significantly from 85 crore rupees a year prior [E25]. Consequently, the debt-to-equity ratio has climbed to 1.28x, meaning debt now exceeds the company's net worth and introduces substantial leverage risk [E23]. Furthermore, shareholders receive no compensation for taking on these financial hazards, as the dividend yield sits entirely at 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: [E8].

Conceded: [E20], [E21], [E22], [E23], [E25], [E37]. While borrowings have risen to Rs 119 Cr [E25] and operating cash flow is negative [E21], the company's underlying operational profitability and capital efficiency remain extraordinarily high with an ROE of 30.62% and ROCE of 28.18% against sector benchmarks of just 5.39% and 6.7% [E8, E9]. Top-line and bottom-line expansions are robust, demonstrating compounded sales growth of 26% and profit growth of 45% over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14], comfortably outpacing the sector median sales growth of 13.3% and profit growth of 17.7% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded consistently over the last four years to reach 16% in March 2026, marking a 6 percentage point increase from three years earlier [E17, E18]. This strong fundamental performance is underpinned by a supportive sector tailwind score of +0.63 in Services [E43, E44]. Finally, despite the lack of a dividend yield [E3], the market price of Rs 164 sits below the discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 232, providing a 29.3% margin of safety [E31, E32], with today's price implying only 5.2% earnings growth against a 10.0% base case [E33].

Conceded: [E13], [E14], [E17], [E18], [E43], [E44]. While the bull highlights rapid top-line growth and expanding margins [E13, E17], these reported earnings gains completely vanish into thin air when evaluated against the severe cash generation collapse of -0.50x and negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -12 Cr [E20, E21, E22]. The impressive statutory returns [E8, E9] ring hollow in the face of dangerously high debtors stretching to 349 days [E37], which explains why profits are failing to materialize as actual cash in the bank. Furthermore, this cash starvation is actively forcing the company deeper into debt, with total borrowings escalating from Rs 85 Cr to Rs 119 Cr and driving the debt-to-equity ratio to a precarious 1.28x where liabilities explicitly exceed net worth [E23, E25]. Finally, relying on a theoretical discounted cash flow valuation [E31, E32] ignores the glaring reality that the stock yields a meager 0.00% in dividends [E3] and sits depressed at just 27% of its 52-week range [E4].
